community.description.text: Where to talk about SAIPEN, where to file bugs, and how to propose a protocol change.

community.discuss.body.text: The SAIPEN Community on Discord: quick questions, screenshots, rough ideas and cross-project feedback.

community.report.body.text: Reproducible bugs and durable feature requests belong in GitHub Issues, so they do not disappear into chat history. Each ecosystem project has its own tracker.

community.contribute.body.text: SAIPEN is a specification first: most contributions change the protocol documents, a phase file or the conformance tooling. Read the contributing guide before proposing a change.

community.proposal.intro.text: Every idea is first run through the litmus test:

community.proposal.q1.text: Does it make the transition between agents more reliable?

community.proposal.q2.text: Does it make the behaviour of different models more uniform?

community.proposal.q3.text: Does it reduce the probability of context loss?

community.proposal.body.text: Two "no" answers put it out of scope for the protocol, however useful it is elsewhere. A good report names the file and section, shows concrete evidence — a quote, a command and its output, a breaking scenario — and says what you expected instead. Normative changes need a changelog entry and, where practical, validator or scenario coverage, and the canonical validator (`python tools/validate.py`) must pass.

community.decided.intro.text: These were proposed and evaluated before; reopening them needs new evidence, not a new request:

community.decided.consensus.text: turning SAIPEN into a distributed consensus system;

community.decided.grammar.text: a machine-parseable LOG marker grammar beyond the existing line skeleton;

community.decided.doctor.text: a `saipen doctor` command that would duplicate `validate` and `status`.

community.conduct.body.text: The project's [code of conduct]({conduct}) applies in the repository and in the community channels.
